title: Review reinterpret-cast assumptions
why: reinterpret_cast can depend on alignment, aliasing, lifetime, pointer provenance, or calling-convention assumptions. Some uses, including valid byte views, are intentional; this advisory identifies code to review rather than proving undefined behavior.
suggestion: Check the source and destination types and subsequent use. Validate alignment, lifetime, bounds, and any function-call signature; prefer typed access, memcpy, or bit_cast where their semantics fit, and retain justified low-level conversions.
limitations: Matches reinterpret_cast syntax outside comments and quoted or raw string literals, including a line break before the opening angle bracket; does not resolve source or destination types, aliases, macro expansion, bounds checks, or subsequent dereferences.

Byte-view casts remain review evidence: a char or byte destination alone does not establish an object-pointer source, valid lifetime, or bounded access. Integer-to-pointer, function-pointer, and alignment-sensitive conversions are not excluded.

One advisory per rule and file, located at the first matching cast line; related_files preserves every other distinct matching source line. The count describes evidence lines, not defects or individual casts.
